gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Renogy sells two different 12V 3000W REGO inverter chargers with different shore-power limits: the HF split-phase model RIV1230RCH-SPS takes single-phase 120V (90–140V AC) or split-phase 120/240V (180–280V AC) input with a 50A maximum bypass at 120V AC, while a REGO 3000W quick manual says the AC source must be 30A or less or the inverter will not work and limits the AC load center to 30A.
standout_why: I read the cited Victron article 'How to Size a Solar System for Your RV' (2026-05-04). It names SmartSolar/BlueSolar MPPT, Cerbo GX, the VE.Direct Bluetooth dongle, Lynx Distributor, MPPT WireBox and SmartSolar Control, and its compatibility notes are about which charge controllers have Bluetooth and which work with the SmartSolar Control display. It says nothing about shore-power amperage, split phase or transfer-switch ratings, and it names no inverter model. I could not read the other cited page, Renogy's 'RV Inverter Installation Guide': WebFetch returned only the site menu, and later requests to renogy.com returned HTTP 429. So I can't rule out that it mentions 30A/50A shore power. None of the result titles suggest it.
decides: The answer's top integrated pick, 'Renogy REGO 12V 3000W Pure Sine Wave Inverter Charger', is the RIV1230RCL-1SS, listed today at $989.99 rather than the $949.00 ChatGPT showed. Its product page mentions an 'integrated transfer relay' but gives no amp rating. The relay's limit decides the pick for RVs on 50A (120/240V split-phase) shore power: Renogy's own HF manual gives the RIV1230RCH-SPS a 50A bypass and an accepted split-phase input range, which makes it the REGO to check for a 50A coach. A 30A coach is covered by either. The 'AC source ≤30A' manual I found does not name its model, so the RCL's own limit still needs confirming from its manual before the page states it.

findings.value: DC Home app over Bluetooth; Renogy ONE Core or ONE M1 for long-range monitoring (sold separately); RMS-P2 wired remote (included); RV-C network supported
findings.source_title: Renogy REGO HF Inverter Charger 3000W RIV1230RCH-SPS User Manual (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: The parts list calls for 400 A ANL fuses, 4/0 AWG battery cable and a 6 AWG grounding cable. Page 8 restriction: 'The BTS port can only be used with lead-acid batteries.'

findings.product: Renogy REGO 12V 3000W Inverter Charger (quick manual, model not printed on the page I read)
findings.label: Shore power / generator source limit and AC output limit
findings.value: AC source current must be 30 A or less or the inverter will not work; AC load center 30 A max; 30 A output circuit breaker; AC input cable at least 10 AWG; 400 A battery fuse
findings.source_title: Renogy REGO Quick Manual, 'REGO Inverter Charger 3000W Version A0' (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: The source line is in Chinese: '请确保AC电源电流≤30A，否则逆变器无法工作' (make sure the AC supply current is 30 A or less, otherwise the inverter cannot work). The page does not print a model number, so I have not tied it to RIV1230RCL-1SS. It also says the inverter supports 12V batteries only, and not to use the temperature sensor on an LFP battery that has a BMS.
